macro_synthesis.headline_zh: 黄仁勋闪电辞职重塑AI算力锚，美分裂国会与华绿能出海主导跨市场分化
macro_synthesis.executive_summary: 本期《经济学人》（2026年11月12日至14日）揭示了四大改写全球资产定价锚的宏观与产业剧变。第一，AI算力链突发治理与地缘“双黑天鹅”：执掌英伟达33年的黄仁勋因涉华算力走私客户丑闻闪电辞职，风暴直指美国商务部长卢特尼克，叠加软银NAV暴跌敲响一级市场AI去杠杆警钟，美股AI硬件彻底告别单一GPU垄断溢价并加速向定制化ASIC切换，而BIS极端鹰派化将倒逼A股算力与光刻胶材料进入极限全栈国产替代。第二，中国碳排放越过历史峰值并加速下行，并非源于气候利他主义，而是由全面电气化与压降70%成本的“绿色技术通缩”驱动；中国光储及EV借道东南亚与南非市政私有化狂飙出海，实质性对冲欧美关税壁垒，在长期压制全球原油与海运煤远期曲线的同时，确立中国电网设备与出海龙头的估值重估。第三，2026年美国中期选举民主党重夺众议院，选民在州级公投中摒弃1.83亿美元文化战争噪音、跨党派倒向最低工资上调与医保扩张，分裂国会与刚性用工成本将驱动美股向阳光地带公用事业、政府医保与折扣零售防御轮动。第四，消费与传媒呈极致“杠铃化”，中国平价连锁加盟模式与AI动态定价正重塑全球大众消费ROIC版图。

us_market_overview.overall_stance: 短期高位承压、高Beta算力去杠杆与防御价值轮动加剧
core_drivers: 黄仁勋闪电辞职引爆英伟达“关键人断层”与商务部BIS出口管制冻结危机，叠加软银高杠杆AI资产净值跳水，触发美股通用GPU算力链估值倍数（P/E）收缩与高Beta科技股去杠杆。
2026中期选举后美国进入“分裂国会”双轨博弈，众议院连环传票调查抬升政策波动率；各州公投跨党派通过最低工资上调与医保扩围，刚性推升服务业用工成本但托底大众必需消费。
全美“蓝州加税、红州吸金”的州际制度套利在佛罗里达逆势深红化中进一步固化，叠加影视传媒“杠铃化”裂变与AI动态定价监管恐慌退潮，资金加速向具备高自由现金流的确定性龙头聚拢。

万店平价茶饮零售加盟、高保真潮玩IP、OTA平台及高回购港股互联网蓝筹（契合特许经营高ROIC革命、娱乐杠铃化与AI动态收益管理，代表标的：蜜雪冰城 2097.HK、名创优品 9896.HK/MNSO、泡泡玛特 9992.HK、携程集团 9961.HK、腾讯控股 0700.HK）

cross_market_chains.chain_title: AI算力治理黑天鹅与出口管制极化传导链
cross_market_chains.economist_trigger: 黄仁勋因涉华走私客户Megaspeed丑闻闪电辞职并波及美商务部长卢特尼克，叠加软银NAV暴跌与日本前首相福田康夫逝世后的中日关系深冻。
cross_market_chains.macro_channel: 核心人物风险（Key-Man Risk）引爆公司治理溢价重估 -> 国会强制接管BIS触发对华芯片与日系材料极限封锁 -> 全球AI资本开支从单一GPU垄断向ASIC多元化与本土全栈闭环裂变。
cross_market_chains.us_mapping: 英伟达（NVDA）与软银系高杠杆芯片股（ARM）遭遇治理折价与去杠杆双杀；资金向博通（AVGO）、迈威尔（MRVL）等ASIC定制芯片及平稳交接的苹果（AAPL）端侧生态迁移。
cross_market_chains.cn_mapping: 灰色转口算力通道彻底焊死，倒逼国内云大厂与智算中心全面转向华为昇腾链、寒武纪（688256.SH）、中芯国际（688981.SH）以及半导体光刻胶/精密机床的极限国产替代。
cross_market_chains.divergence_insight: 美股定价核心在于“垄断溢价破灭与AI商业化ROI证伪下的估值中枢下移”，而A股则将海外极端断供转化为“本土高端算力与设备材料市占率非线性跃升的业绩确定性”。

cross_market_chains.chain_title: 中国碳达峰拐点与“全球南方”绿能出海重估链
cross_market_chains.economist_trigger: 中国碳排放量迎来结构性实质下降，对东盟清洁技术出口创历史新高，且南非执政党ANC地方大选得票率崩盘至31%倒逼市政公用事业私有化。
cross_market_chains.macro_channel: 中国全产业链规模效应输出“绿色技术通缩（成本降逾70%）” -> 破局欧美关税壁垒并激活东南亚/非洲电力基建CapEx -> 全球化石能源长期需求见顶与电网/储能瓶颈溢价凸显。
cross_market_chains.us_mapping: 传统跨国油气与海运煤炭巨头（XOM, CVX, BTU）面临长期远期曲线压制；美国本土缺乏成本竞争力的光伏组件商（FSLR）承压，而电网改造设备（ETN）与铜铝矿企（FCX）受益。
cross_market_chains.cn_mapping: 有效消化国内产能过剩折价，驱动整车出海（比亚迪）、大储与逆变器（阳光电源、德业股份）、特高压配网设备（思源电气、国电南瑞）及绿电核电运营商（中国核电）迎来EPS与P/E戴维斯双击。
cross_market_chains.divergence_insight: 欧美市场将绿能视为“受困于高利率与关税保护的高成本补贴行业”，而中国市场则凭借全产业链绝对成本统治力，在新兴市场将其兑现为“高毛利、高周转的全球基础设施出口红利”。

cross_market_chains.chain_title: 美国中期选举分裂国会与民生实用主义转向链
cross_market_chains.economist_trigger: 民主党重夺众议院开启调查风暴，1.83亿美元跨性别文化战争广告失效，各州公投跨党派通过提高最低工资与扩大Medicaid，佛罗里达稳守深红堡垒。
cross_market_chains.macro_channel: 国会立法极化阻断激进财政扩张 -> 州级直接民主强推劳动报酬再分配与公共医保支出 -> 蓝红州际税基与人口迁徙固化，美国底层服务业通胀粘性与大众消费韧性并存。
cross_market_chains.us_mapping: 劳动密集型餐饮连锁（SBUX, MCD）毛利率受薪资刚性挤压；政府医保托管（UNH, CNC）、仓储折扣零售（COST, WMT）、阳光地带公用事业（NEE）及去政治化主流娱乐（DIS）跑赢大盘。
cross_market_chains.cn_mapping: 美国服务业高用工成本与追求性价比的民生转向，直接利好中国跨境高性价比供应链、商用服务机器人（石头科技、九号公司）以及对美阳光地带出口的电网变压器与园林家居设备（金盘科技、巨星科技）。
cross_market_chains.divergence_insight: 美股消费板块内部承受“人工成本通胀侵蚀利润率”的供给侧痛点，而中国出海制造与智能硬件则作为“通胀平替与降本工具”承接美国中低收入阶层与企业端的刚性外溢需求。

cross_market_chains.chain_title: 全球消费传媒“杠铃化”与数字化供应链革命链
cross_market_chains.economist_trigger: 中国餐饮零售掀起万店特许加盟出海潮，好莱坞Skydance困守影视“危险中间地带”，AI千人千面定价恐慌被证伪，生理周期伪科学向多模态传感演进。
cross_market_chains.macro_channel: AI算法与数字化供应链重构消费服务业成本曲线 -> 行业利润向“零边际成本UGC/极致供应链平价加盟”与“高壁垒顶级实景IP/精准生物传感硬件”两端集中 -> 平庸中型品牌出清。
cross_market_chains.us_mapping: 传统中型影视制片厂（PARA, WBD）与泛健康日历App被边缘化；流媒体与现场体验霸主（NFLX, TKO）、AI智能穿戴龙头（AAPL, GRMN）及动态定价电商/OTA（AMZN, BKNG）实现毛利率扩张。
cross_market_chains.cn_mapping: 平价茶饮与潮流零售加盟龙头（蜜雪冰城、名创优品、古茗）、高保真潮玩实景IP（泡泡玛特）、AI微短剧出海、在线旅游OTA（携程集团）及智能戒指/穿戴ODM供应链（歌尔股份、立讯精密）享受高ROIC溢价。
cross_market_chains.divergence_insight: 美股赢家依托“全球平台算法垄断与超级IP定价权”赚取高毛利溢价，而中资消费与科技龙头则通过“极致数字化供应链周转+轻资产加盟/精密硬件迭代”实现从下沉市场向全球的降维渗透。

core_articles.title: China’s exports of clean tech to South-East Asia are soaring
core_articles.description: Unlike in the European Union, governments don’t fret about the influx
core_articles.lead_excerpt: I n recent years, China’s green-tech manufacturers have salivated over the market for their stuff in Europe. Demand there has surged as countries and consumers try to reduce their reliance on fossil fuels. European governments are becoming fretful about the impact on their industries and are trying to curb the influx, such as by imposing quotas on electric vehicles. But Chinese firms have options closer to home. Their exports to South-East Asia are soaring. Few in the region whinge.
core_articles.zh_title: 中国绿能科技出口狂飙东南亚：破局欧美关税壁垒的“南方增量”与出海重估
core_articles.core_thesis: 面对欧盟对华电动车配额及关税围堵，中国清洁技术制造商正加速向东南亚转移，对东盟光伏、储能及EV出口额创历史新高且当地政府鲜有贸易保护阻力；东南亚工业化电力缺口与本土缺乏竞争性老牌车企的制度结构，使中国廉价绿能设备成为东盟降低化石能源依赖与能源转型成本的最优解；跨市场定价层面，东盟需求有效对冲欧美贸易壁垒引发的产能过剩折价，驱动中国光储及出海整车龙头迎来海外EPS上修与P/E估值修复。
transmission_chain: 一阶冲击：欧盟贸易壁垒升温倒逼中国光伏、锂电与电动车企加速向东盟十国倾注产能与绿地投资，东南亚跃升为中国绿能出口核心增量市场。
二阶传导（利率/监管/供应链/CapEx）：东盟各国推行零关税或本土组装补贴政策吸引中企建厂，不仅消化中国国内冗余产能，更带动区域电网改造与充电基建CapEx周期开启。
美股EPS与估值映射：美股本土光伏与老牌车企在非美新兴市场份额进一步遭中企挤压，海外营收指引面临下修；东南亚互联网与出行平台则受益于廉价EV车队普及带来的UE改善。
A股/港股映射与预期差：市场此前过度定价欧美双反与关税对出口链毛利率的毁灭性打击，忽视了东盟高增速与高毛利整车/组件出口的替代弹性，出海龙头存在显著估值预期差。

core_articles.title: The Bottom Line newsletter: Nvidia will never be the same
core_articles.description: Shailesh Chitnis, our chip-industry expert, reflects on the fall of Jensen Huang
core_articles.lead_excerpt:
Billionaires behaving badly is hardly news. Yet the speed of Jensen Huang’s unravelling stands apart. On November 8th Nvidia’s boss confessed to an affair, after reports linked him to an executive at Megaspeed, one of Nvidia’s customers, who is suspected of smuggling chips into China—and working for Chinese intelligence. Three days later came reports of a second affair, with a subordinate. By November 12th the pressure was too much and Mr Huang resigned, ending a 33-year reign in less than a week. (Reports of a third affair have since surfaced.) When I interviewed Mr Huang in June in Taipei, he told me he was good at “seeing around corners”. Evidently not this one.

It would be hard to devise a more thorough act of self-sabotage. His fall is all the worse because he sold himself as different from other tech moguls. On the trip I spent following him around, I discovered he is treated in Taiwan less as a billionaire than as a local boy made good. His wife and parents were often at his side, adding to his wholesome appeal. The Taiwanese have nicknamed him “the People’s Dad”, a man unchanged by success. As I noted at the time, he had projected that image with care.

Mr Huang inspired fierce loyalty inside Nvidia, too. He was a famously tough boss, known for dressing down senior executives in full view of their colleagues, yet staff regarded him as fair. Mistakes were called out but not punished, so long as they were owned up to promptly. A long-serving executive explained to me that no one at Nvidia is allowed to “fail alone”: when something goes wrong, “it can’t be because only one person knew about it, made a decision, then they go cover it up.” Mr Huang, it seems, held himself to a laxer standard.

Small wonder, then, that the employees I spoke to this week sounded disappointed. Before his resignation, one insisted that it was still business as usual, and Mr Huang’s emails to staff read as though nothing had happened. Few at Nvidia were ready for what came next. The company had no public succession plan and its founder had never nominated an heir. Colette Kress, the finance chief now serving as interim boss, could hardly have imagined taking the job a week ago. For the first time in its history, Nvidia faces a future without Mr Huang.

core_articles.title: A franchise revolution is stirring in China
core_articles.description: It is bringing buzzy retail brands to every corner of the country—and beyond
core_articles.lead_excerpt: Y ang Guofu spent much of the 1990s running from the _chengguan_, a dreaded troop of goons with the authority to rough up street vendors in the name of tidier cities. At the time he was grilling squid from a cart in a north-eastern town. Since then Mr Yang has turned his business into a global restaurant franchise with more than 7,000 outlets. His company, Yangguofu, dishes up a spicy Chinese soup known as _malatang_. Most of its shops are in China, but it has expanded to more than 20 other countries, opening in London and Rome last year, and in Luxembourg last month, far from the reach of the _chengguan_.

core_articles.lead_excerpt: N ot long ago, after a whopping defeat in midterm elections, the president made some conciliatory noises and some belligerent ones. When crisis struck he worked with the House to deliver an historic economic rescue package—even though by then, in a party-line vote, the opposition had impeached him.

core_articles.title: South Africans are giving up on Nelson Mandela’s party. Good
core_articles.description: The decline of the African National Congress shows that democracy is working
core_articles.lead_excerpt: “T hE IMPATIENCE and dissatisfaction among ordinary people are justified,” Nelson Mandela warned his party in 1999. At the time, the African National Congress (anc) utterly dominated South Africa. A generation on, after years of corruption, stagnation and collapsing public services, South Africans have run out of patience entirely. At local elections on November 4th they handed the ruling party its worst-ever result in a nationwide ballot. Though the ANC eked out 31% of all votes, more than any rival, that was less than half of what it recorded in 2004. In the country’s most dynamic places, it did especially badly. It is no longer the largest party in any big city, including Johannesburg, the commercial capital.

core_articles.description: Voters want neither trans kids playing girls’ sports, nor politicians obsessed with it
core_articles.lead_excerpt: T he most effective Republican ad of 2024, many strategists agreed, was one that declared that “Kamala is for they/them” and Donald Trump was “for you”. This year, conservative groups tried to repeat the trick, devoting at least $183m to attack ads on transgender issues, according to AdImpact, a research firm. The strategy failed to protect Republican seats. Yet where trans-related issues were put to voters directly, the response was different.

core_articles.lead_excerpt: W HEN FUKUDA YASUO, a 90-year-old former prime minister of Japan, died last month, China’s supreme leader, Xi Jinping, sent condolences. Mr Fukuda had devoted much of his career to stabilising Sino-Japanese ties. He worked behind the scenes to calm Chinese anger in the early 2000s over the then prime minister’s visits to Yasukuni, the shrine in Tokyo that honours Japan’s war dead, including 14 class-A war criminals. In 2014, when relations had frozen again over the disputed Senkaku Islands, he convinced Mr Xi to meet then-prime minister Abe Shinzo at the Asia-Pacific (APEC) summit in Beijing that year.
